title: DSA - Why Quicksort? + Time Complexity
description:
## Quicksort
Quicksort is the most commonly used sorting algorithm in practice. Like merge sort, it's divide and conquer:

1. Pick a **pivot** element
2. **Partition**: move everything smaller to the left, everything larger to the right
3. Recursively sort left and right sides

### Why not just use merge sort?
- Merge sort needs extra memory for the merge step (O(n) extra space)
- Quicksort sorts **in place** - no extra arrays needed
- Quicksort is faster in practice due to better cache performance

### Time Complexity:
- **Best/Average: O(n log n)** - good pivot splits evenly
- **Worst: O(n²)** - bad pivot (already sorted array with first element as pivot)

### vs Merge Sort:
| | Quicksort | Merge Sort |
|---|---|---|
| Average | O(n log n) | O(n log n) |
| Worst | O(n²) | O(n log n) |
| Space | O(1) in place | O(n) extra |
| Practice | Faster | Slower |
Don't worry, soon you can write it yourself!
